subject: Post-call: ACME discovery & competitive quality tests
messages:
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Ethan Moore <ethan.moore@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 22 Apr 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: ACME discovery & competitive quality tests

Hi Ethan / Tara —

Thanks again for the time this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned: 

Recap (call highlights)
- Primary goal: reduce hallucination-related support incidents for ACME’s internal knowledge assistant while keeping 99th percentile latency under ~250ms for 512-token responses.
- Current constraint: ACME evaluates both the hyperscaler-managed endpoints (HyperscaleCloud AI) and an in-house optimized runtime. Key decision criteria: hallucination rate on knowledge prompts, cost per 1k tokens at production volume, and regional data residency.

Proposed competitive tests (high level)
1) Quality sweep — 1,200 prompts sampling knowledge, multi-step reasoning, and few-shot classification. Track: hallucination rate, F1 on extractive answers, and confidence calibration.
2) Regression checks — run ACME’s two canonical prompts (KB-lookup-01, Summarize-Flow-09) against baseline model on HyperscaleCloud, your in-house runtime, and Redwood hosted runner.
3) Latency/cost spot checks — end-to-end p95/p99 and estimated monthly cost at your projected QPS.
4) Data residency verification — confirm logs and KV cache behavior for VPC/private deploy.

Attachments I’m sending: eval_prompts_v3.xlsx (prompt set), a Redwood vs Hyperscaler matrix template (CSV) for your team to populate if helpful, and a quick data map example (PNG) to show what we’d ask for during an on-prem pilot.

Immediate asks / next steps
- Ethan/Tara: confirm which two production prompts you want prioritized for regression checks.
- ACME security: share preferred SCP/contractor access window for a short test (we’ll need a VPN or short-lived token if you want to run against Private).
- Marissa / Ben: can you take ownership of the test plan and timeline? Suggested run: 4 business days of tests, with an initial results bake at end of day 3.

I’ll schedule a follow-up for next Thursday to review initial deltas and decide whether a dedicated Sanity Pass (longer run) is warranted.

Thanks — talk soon.

—
Sofia Ivanova
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0133
Redwood Inference — Production-first LLM inference

References: HubSpot deal ACME-2026-EXP-47

From: Ethan Moore <ethan.moore@acme-analytics.com>

Date: Wed, 22 Apr 2026 11:03:22 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: ACME discovery & competitive quality tests

Thanks Sofia — very helpful summary. A few clarifications: 

1) Priorities: please prioritize hallucination rate on KB-lookup-01 and the multi-step reasoning prompt (Summarize-Flow-09). Those are driving the top support tickets.
2) Data residency: ACME legal wants logs stored in our us-west region for any hosted test; for Private we’ll expect no outbound telemetry. We’ll confirm the precise language tomorrow.
3) Timeline: we can get the two prompts into your spreadsheet by EOD. Can Redwood provide a short example script to run the CSV prompt set through your hosted endpoints? That’ll help us mirror the test on HyperscaleCloud and our runtime.

Also looping Tara (security) on the access window.

—Ethan
Ethan Moore
Principal Product Manager, ACME Analytics
ethan.moore@acme-analytics.com

Ethan — great, thanks for prioritizing those two prompts. Answers inline and next actions below.

Script + reproducibility
- I attached a small example runner (Python snippet included in the Drive link) that: 1) reads the Excel prompt set, 2) posts to an endpoint with a stable temperature/beam config, and 3) emits a CSV of raw outputs plus a hash for repeatability. That should make it straightforward for your infra team to run the same inputs against HyperscaleCloud and your in-house runtime.

Quality metrics we’ll report back
- Hallucination flag (binary) per answer with brief provenance note when available
- Extractive match rate (F1) where applicable
- Calibration score (confidence vs correctness) for multi-step prompts
- p95/p99 latency and token cost estimate (USD / 1k tokens) per model variant

Operational asks for ACME security
- For hosted Redwood runs: please confirm whether a per-test policy to drop logs after 30 days is acceptable (we can reduce retention to 0 days for private pilots).
- For Private/VPC: provide an internal contact to coordinate VPN/SSH access windows.

Proposed schedule (sample)
- Day 0 (today): finalize prompt set (Ethan) + security window (Tara)
- Day 1: run smoke tests on Redwood hosted + HyperscaleCloud (small sample, 100 prompts)
- Day 2–3: full sweep (1,200 prompts) — record metrics
- Day 4: internal Redwood sanity check + sync call to review deltas

Marissa / Ben — can you confirm you’re OK to run the hosted tests and produce the initial CSV? Ben, I listed you as lead on the private-run coordination in case ACME opts for a VPC pilot.

Thanks — I’ll drop the Drive link and the runner in the follow-up email.

—
Sofia

Looping in an operational note and quick checklist from our infra side —

Ben here. I’ll run the Redwood hosted sweep and produce the CSV export. A couple of details I’ll need:
- Target model variant: recommend starting with redwood-compat-v2 (quantized) and redwood-raw-v1 (no quant). We’ll include HyperscaleCloud’s closest configuration in the matrix.
- Rate limits: we’ll blast at ~10 QPS for the short sweep; if ACME wants a higher concurrency smoke, tell me and I’ll request a temporary quota bump.
- Attachments included: redwood-vs-hyperscaler-matrix.csv (template) and internal test-plan.md (runbook).

I’ll aim to publish interim results by end of Day 3 (UTC). If ACME confirms the private pilot, I’ll coordinate the short-lived VPN token window with your security team and Marissa will own scheduling.
